editorial:
Imagine you are stepping back into the early days of cinema where the action is raw and the hats are big. You get to follow Bill Dane and Banty, two guys who decide they have had enough of the outlaw life and quit Kell's gang. The vibe is a classic tale of redemption and revenge. When Bill stops the gang from stealing a big shipment of gold bullion, he actually ends up becoming the town Sheriff. It is a great setup because you get to see a former criminal trying to do the right thing while his old boss is out there wanting him dead. The tension builds quickly as the old gang returns to take back the gold and throw Bill in a cell.

What really makes this ride fun is the pacing and the role of Tarzan, the horse, who is almost like a main character. The action scenes are straightforward and punchy, though some of the acting feels a bit stiff since it is from 1932. If you love old-school Westerns, you should definitely track this down. Since it is an older film, you might want to look for a restored 4K Blu-ray to add to your physical collection for the best picture quality, or see if you can find a high-def stream on Prime Video for a quick watch.
endingExplained: After escaping his captors, Bill Dane tracks down Kell and his gang for one final showdown. In a high-stakes gunfight, Bill uses his skills to take down the outlaws and save the gold. While Bill fights, his loyal horse Tarzan runs to get help, which ensures the gang cannot escape. Bill wins the fight, clears his name for good, and brings peace back to the town, proving he is a true lawman.
targetAudience: Ideal for anyone who loves old Westerns and stories about outlaws turning good.
